sentence: This project measures biomarkers, including genomic ones, to see how specific therapies affect myelofibrosis, a clonal stem cell disorder.
This project studies how cells move to build craniofacial structures in mouse embryos and how those movements are controlled.
This project supplies biostatistics, bioinformatics and high-performance computing support to cancer research.
This project studies how metabolic syndrome and chronic inflammation relate to gout, using genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics and proteomics together.
This project tests a compound in an animal model for preventing epilepsy after brain injury and looks for biomarkers that predict who develops it.
This project looks for biomarkers in easily collected samples to develop tests that catch high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma early.
This project builds methods to copy and measure how signaling events in cells vary across time and 3D space.
This project uses biochemical engineering to build RNA-targeting tools from human protein parts that retune gene expression.
This project studies how cancer stem cells in squamous cell carcinomas change the tumor microenvironment to help the tumor grow.
This project studies how flexible, disordered regions of proteins organize transcription, RNA processing and DNA repair through nuclear condensates.
This project studies how a receptor linked to prostate cancer and blood pressure works, and looks for small drug-like chemicals that change its activity.
This project studies how the body breaks down liposomes and tests liposomal doxorubicin made with cholesterol analogs for treating cancer.
This project uses whole genome sequence data from people with bipolar disorder to search for genes linked to the disorder.
This project maintains a core facility offering microscopy and electrophysiology services to researchers.
This project tests whether a computer-assisted bilingual vocabulary program helps children with developmental language disorder who are emergent bilinguals.
This project studies how a targeted therapy for aggressive B-cell lymphomas affects T-cell responses in mice and how it can boost immunotherapy.
This project studies how sleep and physical activity interact with genes to affect cardiovascular health, using data from many cohorts and biobanks.
This project studies how inflammation drives atherosclerosis using proteomic profiling, human genetics, bioinformatics and small animal models.
This project tests a home-based respiratory muscle training program to see if it eases shortness of breath in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
This project tests whether adalimumab slows synucleinopathy in people with a sleep behavior disorder, using immune cell studies and brain imaging.
